correctness.rationale: Let f(t)=t/(1+t). The definition of J_2 is sup f(||x+y||) over unit isosceles-orthogonal pairs. The published all-space isosceles representation says the supremum of ||x+y|| over that set is J(X). Since f is increasing and continuous, sup f = f(sup), including when no maximizer exists. Thus \(J_2(X)=J(X)/(1+J(X))\). The definition of J_1 similarly gives min{f(a),f(b)}=f(min{a,b}) pointwise, hence \(J_1(X)=f(J(X))\), proving \(J_1(X)=J_2(X)\). The source's Hilbert value and Theorem 8 bounds are consistent with the identity.

value.rationale: The finding shows that two separately introduced James-type constants with different admissible sets are numerically identical on every Banach space in scope. It replaces the source's coarse J_2 bounds by an exact formula and transfers all J-dependent exact values and threshold properties. This is a structural collapse of an invariant rather than a special-space recomputation or arbitrary slice.
